name: Econfina Creek springs paddle from Walsingham Park
coordinateNote: Entrance or parking coordinates from the November 12, 2026 gap review.
navigationDestination: Walsingham Park, 1047 Walsingham Bridge Road, Chipley, FL 32425 (approach via Porter Pond Road)
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Launch at Walsingham Park and paddle south past the Blue Spring, Williford and Pitt/Sylvan spring areas to the SR 20 bridge, or continue to CR 388 past Gainer Springs. The guide already lists these springs by road and the Gainer paddle below SR 20; this entry is the upper paddle that links them. NWFWMD rates the trip south of Walsingham easy at normal water.
access: Day use 8 a.m. to sunset, seven days. Small paved launch with limited parking; primitive campsite across the bridge (reserve on CampLife). Needs your own boat plus a shuttle or second car to SR 20 (30.4329, -85.5458); a local livery exists but its website did not resolve. No jumping or diving into the creek.

conditions.summary: NWFWMD site page shows no closure notice and FWC lists no notice for Econfina Creek WMA. Creek obstructions after storms are not reported anywhere checked; DEP has previously noted blockages north of Walsingham Bridge (not on this downstream run). (source dated read 2026-11-12)

name: Cotton Landing (Apalachicola National Forest)
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Primitive camping beside a boat ramp on Kennedy Creek, a 4-mile paddle from the Apalachicola River. No toilets or water are listed; it is well off the Wakulla route, so treat it as a later-trip option.
access: No reservation needed. Stay limit: 14 days per month (National Forests in Florida) Derived, not read from the 2026-27 brochure (FWC brochure app errored): rule text says general gun is 'the first 58 days of Zone D antlered deer season'; with FWC's 2026-27 Zone D dates that is Nov 26-29, 2026 and Dec 12, 2026 - Feb 3, 2027. Rule: on National Forest lands camping is 'only on designated campsites during general gun season', so on Nov 26-29 roadside dispersed camping in Apalachicola NF is not legal and a listed hunt camp or campground is the legal choice. Small game season opens the second Saturday of November outside general gun days. Orange requirement not checked; expect armed hunters in camp over Thanksgiving weekend. Forest Service: 'Used as a hunt camp during general gun season.'

conditions.summary: Forest Service page shows 'Site Open' but was last updated before Hurricane Isaias. (source dated 2025-04-11)
